The "request error" rows are calls that fail the same way at any rate. Either
the request is wrong - no such method, a bad argument, a body that does not match
the schema - or
a request refused as larger than accepted, by the target or a proxy in front of it.
Check the config for wallet.v1.Wallet/GetBalance.

A method's percentiles are the time to serve a call: successes, and timeouts
as lower bounds. The rows under it time the other answers:
"overload": the status says overloaded or unavailable (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED,
UNAVAILABLE), from the target or a proxy in front of it; a proxy with no live
backend says the same;
"failure": the status says the call broke (INTERNAL, UNKNOWN, ABORTED and
others), from the target or a proxy in front of it;
"bad response": a reply came and the client did not accept it.

3 requests were cut off by the abort. They are no fault of the target and are
not counted as failures; each is known only to have lasted until the abort.
